text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu-1 reached configured scale limit (48 GPUs). Queue length > 1200 requests, median latency spiking. Severity: P1. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-capacity. Paging ops-oncall.

raj: got it, i'm oncall. pinging infra and prod-eng. first glance: autoscaler metrics show repeated scale-up attempts failing with cloud 429s and image-puller errors.

maya: seen the alert. current impact? any customer-facing errors or 5xxs?

sam: infra here — provider API 429s causing instance create retries. heatmap shows provisioning times jumped from ~90s -> 8-12min. kube nodes stuck in NotReady during init.

elaine: from SRE side: requests are backpressuring frontend -> increased queueing; we have internal throttles but those are nearing downscale thresholds. Customers with heavy streaming calls will see stalls.

carla: customer-success here — I already have one enterprise customer reporting degraded responses for heavy batch embeddings. They'll want ETA to resolution.

raj: immediate plan: 1) divert new ephemeral work to dedicated eu-west-1-dedicated pool (manual routing rule) 2) enable emergency-burst label on a subset of jobs to let them bypass normal batching for latency-critical traffic 3) scale down noncritical background jobs.

sam: starting manual routing change now. applying new routing policy to tag=prod-critical -> eu-west-1-dedicated. command:```sh
# change route
curl -X POST "$REDWOOD_ROUTER/api/v1/routes" -d '{"selector":"tag:prod-critical","target":"eu-west-1-dedicated"}'
```

support-bot: Route change request received and applied by infra. Propagation ~30s.

raj: disabling batch-worker-async queue consumers for 20m to free GPUs for interactive work. doing a graceful drain.

maya: i'm taking the primary troubleshooting lead for autoscaler logic. sam, can you share the autoscaler controller logs? suspect throttling backoff loop.

sam: past 15m: controller reported repeated 429s from cloud provider, then a series of backoff resets. snippet:```text
2026-11-03T02:34:10Z autoscaler controller.go:294 request create vm -> 429 Too ManyRequests
2026-11-03T02:34:12Z autoscaler controller.go:312 backing off for 45s
2026-11-03T02:35:00Z autoscaler controller.go:294 request create vm -> 500 ImagePullBackOff
```

elaine: note — our controller currently tracks 429 as transient and increases backoff aggressively. that's intended but in high sustained demand it prevents eventual progress. need a mitigation.

maya: suggestion: temporarily relax the aggressive backoff threshold for 429s to allow more concurrent create attempts for the next 10m. this is risky but gets capacity online faster. will revert after. raj — approve?

raj: i approve emergency relaxation for 10m. set a timer and monitor.

sam: toggling flag in infra-config:```yaml
autoscaler:
  backoff:
    429:
      enabled: true
      base_delay: 5s
      max_delay: 30s  # lowered from 5m for emergency
```

support-bot: autoscaler flag updated by sam. change id: change-9342.

deploy-bot: Notice: autoscaler controller rolling restart to pick up config change. Pod restart started.

raj: monitoring cluster — nodes appearing, init times improving. queue growth rate slowed from +200s/min to +30s/min.

carla: telling customers: "We're seeing increased provisioning times in eu-west, routing latency-sensitive work to dedicated pool — ongoing mitigation. ETA 15–30m."

david: product here — any fallback option to serve lighter model for queued requests to reduce GPU pressure? can we soft-fail to smaller quantized model for background batches?

maya: yes. adding a temporary model routing rule: large-batch jobs -> model-small-quant; will add header so we can revert.

sam: model routing applied. background job latency improved and queue length flattened.

elaine: we're starting to see error rates normalize. no new customer escalations after carla's notice. continuing to watch for 10m window.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Autoscaler config change observed healthy. Cluster nodes added: +14 GPUs in 6 new nodes.

raj: good work. next steps for post-incident: - root-cause analysis on provider-429 surge and image-pull failures - revisit autoscaler backoff policy w/ safeties (circuit-breaker) - runbook update to include manual routing steps and model-fallback pattern - alert tuning to reduce noise but keep lead indicators. assigning owners: sam (autoscaler/backoff), maya (controller logic & runbook), elaine (oncall playbook & alerts), carla (customer comms post-incident).

maya: taking writeup for the technical postmortem. i'll start a doc and ping for review. timeline: initial writeup in 24h, full postmortem with action items in 72h.

carla: i'll send a customer-facing summary after we have final RCA.

raj: handing off monitoring/cleanup to maya; i'll be available for follow-ups. @maya you're oncall now.

maya: ack, i'm on. closing incident channel in 30m if stable. thanks all. :thumbsup:
